description: Vowel authoring palette. Each vowel is a pattern of resonant peaks (formants). To author a vowel, place a resonance at each formant frequency (F1, F2, and optionally F3). F1+F2 carry the vowel identity; F3 adds presence/naturalness.
source: Peterson & Barney (1952), adult-male averages — the standard acoustic-phonetics reference. Values are approximate; real speech varies by speaker.

voice_scaling.note: Multiply all formant frequencies by these rough factors to shift voice character. Rules of thumb, not exact.

q_guidance.note: Formants are rounded peaks, not razors. Q = frequency / bandwidth. Use the bandwidths below as starting points, then steer by ear.
q_guidance.resulting_Q_range: roughly 4-8 on F1, 15-25 on F2, 15-20 on F3

vowels.shape: low bump + high bump, far apart
two low-mid bumps, close — the open 'ah'
F2 and F3 pulled close together — the 'r' signature

talking_pairs.name: oo -> ee
talking_pairs.motion: F2 flies from 870 up to 2290 — the classic 'oo-ee' glide

talking_pairs.name: ah -> ee
talking_pairs.motion: F1 drops and F2 leaps up — open to bright

talking_pairs.name: oo -> ah
talking_pairs.motion: F1 opens up, F2 rises a little — closed to open

talking_pairs.name: ee -> ah
talking_pairs.motion: F2 collapses down, F1 opens — bright to open
